items.focus: vigorous shaking of liquid in thermally insulated rigid flask
items.sloFit: indirect; original official outcome primarily addresses First Law heat/work and process sign
items.reason: Ideal flask supports negligible heat transfer (adiabatic); nearly fixed volume of contained liquid and rigid container also supports isochoric classification. Those categories are not mutually exclusive, and 'due to' is underspecified.
items.independentRevisionPrinciple: Specify that classification is by heat flow across an insulated boundary, not by constancy of volume; independently authored practice item only after approval.

items.focus: metabolic state while fasting in Ramadan
items.sloFit: weak / indirect; framework does not explicitly require classifying human metabolism as a simple ideal thermodynamic path
items.reason: Fasting alone does not determine whether a selected metabolism/body system follows constant temperature, constant pressure, constant volume, or zero-heat-transfer conditions. The system boundary and constraints are unstated.
items.independentRevisionPrinciple: Use an independently written idealised physical system with specified thermal, volume or pressure constraint; seek separate teacher ruling on any physiological analogy.

items.focus: rigid gas container and internal-energy change after heat input
items.reason: Rigid container eliminates boundary P-dV work; apply First Law with the usual heat-input interpretation of symbol Q. Other work modes are not specified.

items.focus: work done by ideal gas during constant-pressure volume expansion
items.scienceReview: physics and dimensional arithmetic independently checked
items.reason: The printed constant pressure and initial/final volumes define positive work done by gas using W=P(V_f−V_i), with SI pressure and volume units. Printed options include the consistent result.

items.focus: entropy change in solid-to-gas phase transition
items.scienceReview: physics-consistent for the intended phase-change comparison
items.reason: In the listed phase-change alternatives, transfer from solid to gas increases entropy of the material; freezing, crystallisation and condensation normally decrease its entropy.
